office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the state budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing and land-use rules for cities, and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Two Democrats: incumbent Strom Peterson, House Housing chair who also sits on the Snohomish County Council, faces Mukilteo Council President Jason Moon, who pledges to give up his city seat. The race contrasts Peterson's state housing mandates and Millionaire's Tax vote with Moon's calls for local control over density and protecting taxpayers.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative and House Housing Committee chair, also a Snohomish County Councilmember and Edmonds small-business owner, whose record centers rent stabilization, supportive-housing siting and gun-safety laws.
highlights: Chairs the House Housing Committee; co-sponsored 2025 rent stabilization (EHB 1217) [S1][S7]
Prime sponsor of ESHB 2266 (2026), requiring cities to allow supportive housing and shelters [S8][S11]
Co-sponsored and voted for the 2026 Millionaire's Tax [S2][S5]
Campaigns on reproductive freedom and gun-safety laws [S1][S2][S3]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346 and says he was 'proud to cosponsor and vote for the Millionaire's Tax' to fix an 'upside-down' tax code.

spending.basis: Cites nearly a billion dollars for the Housing Trust Fund and investments in behavioral health, transportation and workforce training.

housing.basis: Co-sponsored rent stabilization (7% plus CPI cap), prime-sponsored supportive-housing siting and highlights Housing Trust Fund investment, alongside supply bills.

safety.basis: Emphasizes gun-safety laws and expanded treatment and behavioral-health services rather than enforcement measures.

climate.basis: Voted for the 2025 clean fuels bill; endorsed by Conservation Action and serves on a coal-opposition board; no carbon-pricing statement.

experience.basis: Sitting House committee chair and county councilmember, former Edmonds council president.

local-control.basis: Prime sponsor of a 2026 law requiring local governments to allow supportive housing and shelters in residential areas; cites state middle-housing legislation.

social.basis: Repeated statements defending abortion rights and pledging to fight for LGBTQ neighbors; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for ESHB 1296, which amended and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: Mukilteo City Council President and business partner running as a Democrat on local control of housing density, protecting taxpayers, law-enforcement staffing and full-time representation.
highlights: Says 'state mandated density threatens the character of our communities' and local governments need more control [S1][S2]
Pledges to protect taxpayers from higher taxes: 'It's not a Revenue problem, it's a spending problem' [S2]
Will resign from the Mukilteo City Council if elected; criticizes the incumbent's two offices [S1][S2]

taxes.basis: Pledges leadership 'that protects taxpayers from higher taxes' and says the state has a spending, not revenue, problem.

spending.basis: Calls for balanced, accountable budgeting while protecting essential services.

local-control.basis: Pamphlet and site both oppose state-mandated density and 'top-down' housing mandates and call for more local control.

safety.basis: Says low law-enforcement staffing 'has to change,' while also calling addiction and homelessness system failures.

experience.basis: City council president running on 'fresh perspectives' against a long-serving legislator; has local but not state office.
